Bacterial growth inhibition, broth microdilution MIC
Prepare cation-adjusted Mueller-Hinton broth (CAMHB) and the compound at 2x the top concentration.
Make a 2-fold, 10-point dilution series in broth across the plate.
Carry half the volume from each column into the next, mixing, from column 1 to column 10.
Discard the carried-over volume from the last diluted column, so every well holds the same volume.
Grow the strain to log phase and dilute it in broth to the inoculum density (2x final).
Add an equal volume of inoculum to every well except the sterility control.
Add an equal volume of inoculum to the compound columns and the growth control.
Change the tip between columns, so compound is not carried back into the inoculum.
Mix each well after adding the inoculum.
Read turbidity (OD590 / OD530) or score visible growth; MIC = lowest concentration with no growth.
Cell viability / proliferation, luminescent cellular ATP (CellTiter-Glo type)
Grow the cell line in its growth medium and resuspend it at the seeding density.
Dispense cells into the assay plate.
Let adherent cells attach before adding compound.
Make the compound series in DMSO: 10 points, 1:3, top 40-50 uM.
Add nanolitres of compound, DMSO alone, or the positive control to the cells.
Add nanolitres of each compound concentration in DMSO to the test wells.
Add the same volume of DMSO alone to the vehicle-control wells.
Incubate cells with compound at 37 C, 5% CO2.
Equilibrate the plates to room temperature.
Add CellTiter-Glo reagent (lyses cells; luciferase reads ATP).
Incubate at room temperature for the signal to stabilise.
Biochemical kinase activity, luminescent ADP detection (ADP-Glo type)
Make the compound concentration series in DMSO (about 3-fold steps, 9 points, top 10-46 uM).
Incubate for the luminescent signal to develop.
Read luminescence on a plate reader.
Dispense nanolitre volumes of each compound concentration into the assay plate (pin tool or acoustic transfer).
Add kinase and peptide substrate in kinase buffer (HEPES or Tris pH 7.5, 10 mM MgCl2, EGTA, detergent).
Start the reaction with ATP (at a concentration chosen for the kinase).
Dispense the ATP solution into every well.
Where the peptide substrate is not already in the enzyme mix, add it together with the ATP.
Add ADP-Glo reagent to stop the reaction and deplete the remaining ATP.
Add Kinase Detection Reagent, which converts ADP to ATP and reads it with luciferase.
The reagent converts the ADP formed to ATP, which the luciferase reaction turns into light.

Centre the series on the measured potency of the compound's structural analogs, not on the template's generic default: the top concentration should be the analogs' median IC50 times the series' own centring multiplier (dilution_factor ** ((n_points - 1) / 2)), within one dilution step. The multiplier follows from the half-above / half-below rule plus the template's shape; the AGM states no numeric multiplier of its own (TODO(final): the "100x the expected IC50" rule of thumb is a heuristic, not an AGM number). Derived deterministically by agent/anchor.py, which records which analogs it used; a proposal may depart from it with a stated reason.

Centre the series on the expected IC50: about half the points above it and half below, with full top and bottom plateaus. Checked as: the expected IC50 (potency prior) lies within two dilution steps of the series' log midpoint.
For GPCR antagonists in a cAMP assay, stimulate with agonist at EC50-EC80, within the linear range of the cAMP standard curve; Gi-coupled receptors need forskolin to raise cAMP first.

Test the assay's DMSO tolerance and keep every well at the same final DMSO. Enzyme and binding assays often tolerate 5-10%; cell-based assays usually only up to 0.5% (the cAMP chapter says most cells tolerate up to 1%: the two chapters differ, so check the cell line).
Space concentrations evenly on a log scale, 3-fold or half-log (3.16-fold) steps.
Fit concentration-response data with the four-parameter logistic; fix the top or bottom only when the compound's potency puts that plateau outside the tested range.
Measure under initial-velocity conditions, i.e. less than 10% of the substrate converted.
Luciferase-coupled readouts are prone to luciferase inhibitors: confirm actives with a counterscreen or an orthogonal (non-luciferase) assay.
Each plate needs both a Max and a Min signal control (e.g. vehicle and no-enzyme / reference inhibitor at a saturating concentration), so Z' and percent inhibition can be computed.
A concentration-response curve needs at least 8 concentrations; more concentrations (up to 12) are better than more replicates.
Use at least 10 inhibitor concentrations for an enzyme IC50.
Run at least one control (reference) compound in every run, ideally as potent as the best compound available, and track its potency over runs.
Report an IC50 only if maximum inhibition exceeds 50%, top and bottom are within 15% of theory, and the 95% confidence limits span no more than 2-5 fold.
Potency must be reproducible between runs (minimum significant ratio, MSR, at most 3); if not, add concentrations, replicates or repeat runs (each compound once per run on 2 or more runs).
To detect competitive inhibitors, run at substrate concentrations at or below Km; for kinases, ATP around or below its Km ([S] = Km detects all mechanisms).
An IC50 cannot be measured below half the enzyme concentration (tight binding): keep the enzyme concentration well below the expected IC50.
In competition binding, use the labelled ligand at or below its Kd and keep less than 10% of it bound (no ligand depletion).
Include vehicle (DMSO) wells: the "Max" signal with no test compound, which normalisation needs.
Accept a plate only if Z' >= 0.4 (or signal window >= 2).
